title: Past perfect continuous (I had been doing)
subtitle: I had been doing
summary: Use the past perfect continuous (had been + -ing) for an activity that was in progress before a moment in the past.

lesson.heading: Study this situation
lesson.text: Yesterday morning I got up and looked out of the window. The sun was shining, but the ground was very wet. **It had been raining.** It was not raining when I looked out of the window - the sun was shining. But it had been raining *before*. **had been -ing** is the past perfect continuous.

examples.text: The ground was wet. **It had been raining.**

lesson.heading: An activity before a past moment
lesson.text: We use the past perfect continuous for something that had been happening before a time in the past. Often it explains a past result, like dirty hands or tiredness.

examples.text: My hands were dirty because **I'd been repairing** my bike.
Tom was tired when he got home. **He'd been working** hard all day.
I went to Madrid a few years ago and stayed with a friend of mine. **She hadn't been living** there very long, but she knew the city very well.
**We'd been playing** tennis for about half an hour when it started to rain heavily.
examples.note: something had been happening before something else happened

left.label: Present perfect continuous
examples: I hope the bus comes soon. **I've been waiting** for 20 minutes. (before now)
James is out of breath. **He's been running.** (= he has been running)

right.label: Past perfect continuous
right.text: Up to a moment in the past.
examples: At last the bus came. **I'd been waiting** for 20 minutes. (before the bus came)
James was out of breath. **He'd been running.** (= he had been running)

left.label: Past continuous (was -ing)
examples: It wasn't raining when we went out. The sun **was shining**.

right.label: Past perfect continuous (had been -ing)
examples: But **it had been raining**, so the ground was wet.
She was tired because **she'd been working** hard.

lesson.heading: Verbs not used in continuous forms
lesson.text: Some verbs (for example **know**) are not normally used in continuous forms (be + -ing). With these verbs use the past perfect simple, even for a long period.

examples.text: We were good friends. We **had known** each other for years.
A few years ago Lisa cut her hair really short. I was surprised because **she'd always had** long hair.

lesson.text: was -ing tells you what was happening at the moment; had been -ing tells you what had been going on before that moment and explains the situation you found.

exercises.prompt: Tom was very tired when he got home. ___ hard all day.
exercises.explanation: The working happened before he got home and explains his tiredness: He'd been working.

exercises.prompt: The children came into the house. They had a football and they were both very tired. ___ football.
exercises.explanation: An activity before they came in: They'd been playing football.

exercises.prompt: I was disappointed when I had to cancel my holiday. ___ to it.
exercises.explanation: The looking forward went on before the cancellation: I'd been looking forward to it.

exercises.prompt: Is the activity before now (present perfect continuous) or before a moment in the past (past perfect continuous)?

items.text: I hope the bus comes soon. I've been waiting for 20 minutes.
At last the bus came. I'd been waiting for 20 minutes.
James is out of breath. He's been running.
James was out of breath. He'd been running.
Tom was tired. He'd been working hard all day.
I'm running a marathon next month. I've been training every day.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to say that the tennis game was interrupted by rain.
exercises.answer: We'd been playing tennis for about half an hour when it started to rain.
exercises.explanation: had been -ing for the activity in progress, past simple (started) for the event that interrupted it.

exercises.prompt: James was on his hands and knees on the floor. ___ for his contact lens.
exercises.explanation: He was in the middle of looking at that moment, so the past continuous: He was looking.

exercises.prompt: Sue was sitting on the ground. She was out of breath. ___
exercises.explanation: She had stopped running; the earlier activity explains why she was out of breath: She'd been running.

exercises.statement: We were good friends. We had been knowing each other for years.
exercises.explanation: We had known each other for years. Know is not used in continuous forms.

exercises.prompt: I had arranged to meet Tom in a restaurant. ___ for 20 minutes when I realised that I was in the wrong restaurant.
exercises.explanation: Waiting was in progress before I realised: I'd been waiting for 20 minutes.

exercises.prompt: I was sad when I sold my car. ___ for a very long time.
exercises.explanation: Have for possession is not used in continuous forms, and the time is before a past moment: I'd had it.

exercises.statement: I was sad when my local cafe closed. I'd been going there for many years.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Going there was a repeated activity before the cafe closed, so had been -ing is right.

exercises.prompt: I had arranged to meet Kate, but I was late. When I finally arrived, ___ for me. She was annoyed because ___ such a long time.
options: she was waiting / she'd been waiting
she'd been waiting / she was waiting
she was waiting / she was waiting
exercises.explanation: At the moment I arrived she was still waiting (was waiting); the long wait before that explains her annoyance (she'd been waiting).
